prompt: Plot 300-dimensional customer feature vectors on a 2D chart to see whether natural groups exist.
why: Project onto the top two principal components for a quick look.
trap: Clustering finds groups; PCA lets you see the data first.

prompt: A model has 80 features, many highly correlated with each other, causing unstable coefficients.
why: Principal components are uncorrelated; regress on a handful of them.
trap: Switching to trees sidesteps it but loses the linear model you wanted.

prompt: Compress 1,000 sensor readings per sample into a few numbers that keep most of the variation.
why: Keep the top components explaining, say, 95% of variance.
trap: Clustering would reduce each sample to one label, losing detail.

prompt: Find a small set of basic patterns from which thousands of aligned face images can be approximately rebuilt.
trap: Clusters give typical faces, not building blocks to combine.

prompt: A 60-question survey has answers that move together in a few bunches. Summarize it with a handful of underlying scores.
why: Principal components capture the shared variation in a few dimensions.
trap: Clustering groups respondents; this compresses the questions.

prompt: Training on 5,000 gene-expression features is slow and overfits. Reduce dimensions while keeping most information.
tells: Reduce dimensions while keeping most information
why: Project onto the top components before modeling.
trap: A fancier model doesn't solve having far more features than samples.

prompt: Interest rates for 10 maturities move together; analysts want the 2–3 independent movements that explain almost all daily changes.
tells: 2–3 independent movements that explain almost all
why: The first components are the classic level, slope and curvature.
trap: It's time-indexed, but the question is about structure, not forecasting.

prompt: Show 768-dimensional text embeddings on a scatter plot to eyeball whether topics separate.
why: Project to 2D with PCA (t-SNE and UMAP are non-linear alternatives).
trap: Clustering labels points; it doesn't give you 2D coordinates.
